summary.headline: Gala Precision Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue ~INR75 crore (+20% YoY), EBITDA margin 16.51%, PAT margin 11.44%; FY27 EBITDA margin guided 17-19%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about INR75 crore, up 20% YoY, with EBITDA of about INR12 crore (+28% YoY, 16.51% margin) and net profit of about INR8 crore (+29% YoY, 11.44% margin). Management said order booking rose about 40% YoY and first-quarter revenue is typically 20-22% of the full year. A roughly INR3 crore dispatch slipped out of the quarter due to a customer payment delay, which management said cost about 5 percentage points of growth. Management reiterated 20-25% FY27 revenue growth and a 17-19% EBITDA margin range, and said FY27 working capital would stay at similar levels (around 180 days) pending a KPMG study. The call also covered a Chennai ramp-up, a planned Wada land purchase, and a reduction in forex hedging cover from 70% to 40% of export collections.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR80-85 crore same period last year

segments.name: Disc Springs (DSS)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 54% of Q1 FY27 revenue, sales +31% YoY, growth attributed mainly to the Wada plant. Disc springs are a niche category with customer buying of INR5-10 crore each.

segments.name: SFS
segments.commentary: Contributed 29% of revenue, INR223 million. Management cited growing customer adoption and new business wins; the SFS cost spread versus European peers was described as 10-15% (up to 18%) on exports and 2-3% in India.

segments.name: CSS
segments.commentary: Contributed 17% of revenue, INR125 million, citing steady demand across industrial and mobility applications.

segments.name: Fasteners (Chennai)
segments.commentary: New Chennai plant (4,600 MT installed capacity, high-tensile bolts) is ramping; Phase 1 utilisation about 70-80% in Q1. Wind-turbine fastener contribution is about 25-26% of Q1 sales as stated, with the offshore-wind product targeted at 10% of FY27 fastener sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 17-19%; management said it is confident and that this range holds for FY28 as well.
FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25% YoY; management said it is on track or exceeding this.
Effective tax rate expected at around 20% or less, helped by deductions and a solar open-access project due for commissioning in Q3.
Working capital expected at similar levels (around 180 days) for now; KPMG study report expected by end-August 2026, with targets to be set in Q3.
Chennai Phase 1 utilisation targeted at 80-90% in Q2 and ~70% for Phase 1-2 combined by Q4; Chennai EBITDA expected to be comparable with Wada around Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
New Wada land (10-11 acre) capex of about INR40-45 crore, mostly in FY28, subject to completing the purchase (2-3 months).
capex_capacity: Chennai plant: new fastener facility with 4,600 MT installed capacity; Phase 1 utilisation ~70-80% in Q1 FY27; Phase 2 mezzanine (~10,000 sq ft) construction to finish in Q2 and more machines by Q3, required in Q4.
Chennai monthly run rate: manufacturing INR4-5 crore per month; June production ~INR4.5 crore but dispatches lower due to an item on hold.
Hot-dip galvanising (HDG) plant commissioned at Chennai, brought in-house to improve margin and delivery.
MoU signed for ~10.15 acre of land at Wada, adjacent to existing plant; ~50,000 sq ft shed planned mainly for fasteners and partly disc springs; legal due diligence underway.
Solar open-access project initiated, expected commissioning in Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: Order booking up ~40% YoY, per management.
Pricing stable; management says it offers 10-20% savings to customers while holding margins, and passes through raw-material increases with a lag.
Fasteners cited as the main growth driver. Customer wallet sizes: fasteners INR50-500 crore vs disc springs INR5-10 crore.
New products (bolts, smart fasteners for offshore wind, wedge lock washers) are ~30-35% of order book, per management.
Company said it is taking share from European producers; some multi-year accounts grew share of business from 5-10% to 50-75%.
Forex: forward cover on export collections reduced from 70% to 40% due to euro volatility and war-related uncertainty; ~4% of 12-month exposure already covered.
Product mix: ~85% customised products; ~15% sold to fastener distributors at company level. Disc spring and Gallock 75-80% to OEMs; SFS >95% direct to OEMs.
Management said a single ~INR3 crore+ dispatch was held because of a customer payment delay; ex-this, growth would have been ~25%.
Management cited TAM of USD100 billion for fasteners, with Gala addressing ~USD2.5 billion including bolts and nuts.
Seatbelt retractor spring: customer approved Gala as source after July visit; small-batch supply to start, slow ramp due to safety-critical nature.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin bridge from 16.51% to the 17-19% guide, across forex, Chennai leverage and mix? Also, why cut forward cover from 70% to 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY27 EBITDA margin should be 17-19% with no forex hit since exports are hedged. Jalan cited Chennai utilisation improving in Q3/Q4 and Q1 being ~20-22% of full-year revenue to absorb fixed overheads. The cut to 40% reflects euro volatility and war-related uncertainty; about 4% of 12-month exposure is covered so far.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 growth stack up, and what drove the Q1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Order booking up ~40% YoY. A ~INR3 crore+ dispatch was held for a customer payment delay; ex this, growth would have been ~25%. Management said it is confident of meeting or exceeding the 20-25% FY27 growth guide. DSS growth came from Wada and fastener growth from Chennai.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook, and when will KPMG study benefits show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is expected to stay at similar levels (around 180 days). The KPMG study started in July, with the report expected by end-August or in Q2; targets and actions to be set in Q3, so no firm improvement guidance yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why don't customers switch to Gala despite a 15-18% cost advantage over European peers, and how long does onboarding take?
qa_highlights.answer: Onboarding takes 12-24 months (plant approval, audit, samples, then share-of-business ramp). Some multi-year accounts grew share from 5-10% to 50-75%. Some customers with cost advantage still do not switch immediately. No customer lost on quality or delivery in 25 years.

qa_highlights.question: Seatbelt retractor spring status, land capex timing, and effective tax rate sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Customer approved Gala as source after a July visit; small-batch supply starts with a slow ramp given safety-critical use. Wada land (~10 acre MoU, 2-3 months to close) needs ~INR40-45 crore capex, mostly in FY28. ETR guided at ~20% or less, helped by 100% deductions for R&D (Sec 35(1)(i)), ESOP perquisite deduction, higher tax depreciation and a solar open-access project commissioning in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Chennai utilisation, run rate, and HDG plant impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 utilisation was ~70-80% in Q1 and is targeted at 80-90% in Q2, with Phase 1-2 combined ~70% by Q4. Chennai manufacturing runs at INR4-5 crore a month; June output was ~INR4.5 crore but dispatches were lower due to a held item. In-house HDG improved margin and delivery and unlocked some customers.

risks_watch: Customer payment delays: a ~INR3 crore+ dispatch slipped out of Q1, costing ~5 percentage points of growth; watch Q2 receivables and working capital days versus ~180 days.
Chennai ramp execution: Phase 1 utilisation must reach 80-90% in Q2 and Phase 2 machines are needed by Q4; Chennai EBITDA parity with Wada is guided only for Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
Forex: export hedge cut from 70% to 40% with only ~4% of 12-month exposure covered; euro volatility and war-related risk could affect realisations.
KPMG working capital study (report due end-Aug/Q2) and promised Q3 targets; no quantified working-capital target yet.
Margin guide 17-19% depends on Q3/Q4 Chennai utilisation and the solar project commissioning in Q3 to keep ETR near 20%.
Wind-turbine offshore product ramp: management targets ~10% of FY27 fastener sales, but says current volumes are very small; seatbelt retractor spring ramp expected to be slow.
key_quotes: So as of now, we are quite reasonably confident that we will be achieving 17% to 19%.
So basically, the order booking for -- as I mentioned in the opening talk, order booking is 40% higher as compared to last quarter year -on-year.
And in last 25 years, we never lost a customer also because of either quality or delivery reason.
So, I think firm order booking INR110 crores plus additional schedules which we get every month for dispatch to these customers.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on FY27 guidance (17-19% EBITDA margin, 20-25% revenue growth) and order momentum, but cautious on near-term items: working capital has no firm target until the KPMG study, Chennai ramp is still short of optimum, and the Q1 dispatch shortfall was attributed to a customer payment delay. Answers on forex, tax and capex timing were direct; on the 3-digit revenue question, the CFO declined to give a number.

adds.what: Chennai Phase 2 mezzanine (~10,000 sq ft) and more machines for fastener plant (4,600 MT installed capacity Phase 1 plant ramping)
New Wada land (10-11 acre, ~50,000 sq ft shed mainly fasteners, partly disc springs)
Solar open-access project (power, not production capacity)

growth.why: Management held FY27 revenue growth guidance at 20-25% (midpoint 22.5%), backed by order book up ~40% YoY to ~INR110 crore, Chennai ramp to ~70% Phase 1-2 utilisation by Q4, and a planned Wada expansion of INR40-45 crore mostly in FY28.
